title: Five years of weekends at Christy's
summary: Boston visiting musicians jam at Christy's after-hours sessions.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: So you were playing up in Christie's.
And how long did that last?
Well, I played up there about five years, man.

Weekends, yeah. I would play there because... Most of the time, if I didn't have nothin' to do, I'd just play up there. He told me, like, to make it my home, because he was tickled to death to have me come up. And all the guys used to come out there; you know, all the guys, that would be playing at the Hi-Hat in Boston, they would come to Christie's after they'd get off of work, and we'd jam all night and all that. So we'd have Wardell Gray and Clark Terry, and several other guys that we liked, or that played well -- I'll put it that way. We liked them also. Illinois Jacquet, he was there, too, and Billy Eckstine, Sarah Vaughn... All the people used to come out there. The real artists that was playing at the Hi-Hat or something like that, or in that neighborhood.
Whoever was in the Boston area.
Yeah, whoever was in the Boston area would come out and sit in, you know, and play. We'd throw a party and play for them, and Eddie would give them all that they
wanted to drink, and so forth. So we used to have a ball out at Christy's, yeah. It was very nice.
You say that lasted about five years.
So would you say roughly '51 to '56.
